narrative.overview:
The farm app is a climate-controller dashboard in the category standard: a neutral dark ground, one blue accent, status colour that means something, and numbers set like instruments. It sits beside Grafana, Home Assistant, Vercel/Linear and Ubiquiti UniFi, the four products the owner named as the craft bar, and it aims at their finish rather than at a look of its own. A room's state has to be legible in one glance, at a desk or on a phone at the room door, so decoration never stands in for state.

Density is moderate and calm: cards on a quiet page, hairlines rather than boxes, a tight type scale with tabular figures, plain English and metric units in every line. Colour is spent on state and, by a deliberate exception, on the identity of the three measured quantities. Dark is the default (the owner's choice); a light theme mirrors it token for token.

Scope: every page uses these tokens. The room page (`#/rooms/:id` and its tabs) was rebuilt in this world on 2026-10-28 and every page since (Today, Calendar, Harvest, the task grid) was built in it; the Rooms list is folded into the Overview. (2026-11-05, design-system audit) Some parts built before the components below were written down still differ from them in small ways: a few type sizes and corners off the scale, three chip styles where one is meant, section card titles a step large on some pages. They are listed in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-design-system-css-pass.md`; until that pass, the words here are the target, not the stray CSS. A new page uses the components here as they are, before inventing one.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral dark ground (`page` under `surface` cards), light theme mirroring it.
One blue accent: selection, the primary action, and "running".
Green in band, amber warning, red fault; series hues only on temperature, humidity and CO₂ traces.
One card level; hairline-separated sections inside a card.
Inter, self-hosted, with tabular figures and a tight scale (12 to 32 px).
Status pills, segmented controls, underline tabs.
Metric units, plain English, one number format everywhere.

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Everywhere outside the measured series, colour means state: blue is selection, primary action and running; green is in band; amber is warning; red is fault. Icons, headings, links in prose and target labels stay neutral (the Crop tab's target icons are `muted`). The pictures (below) are the one other exception: they draw things in the room drawing's own colours, never a state colour.

rules.name: The Series Identity Rule
rules.body: (2026-10-28: energy and water have their own hues too.) Temperature, humidity and CO₂ keep their own hues (`--s-t`, `--s-rh`, `--s-co2`) on the reading-card traces and the History charts. This deliberately adapts the category standard's "nothing else coloured": the hue carries a metric's identity from the Now tab to the History tab, which is a data job, not decoration. A series hue never marks state, never fills a button and never colours text other than a chart's own legend. (2026-11-03, owner: "icon") Each reading also has a line icon in its hue beside its name, the same everywhere: a thermometer, a drop, CO₂ bubbles (`web/icons.js`) on the Now tab's reading cards, the Overview's room cards, the History charts' titles and the Outdoor card, where dew point (no chart) takes `ink-2`. (2026-11-04) Harvest kg has its own hue too, `--s-harvest`, a muted ochre (dark `#b8844e`, light `#a87a4c`): the bars of the Harvest page's chart and the Overview card's strip, never state, never text.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Dark is the default (`data-theme="dark"`, stored per browser); the light theme redefines every token under the same name and adds nothing else except a 1 px card shadow. A new colour means a new token in both theme blocks.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or line up (readings, bands, kWh, RM, timestamps, table cells) sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Near-Edge Rule
rules.body: (2026-10-28, owner: amber on a reading the machines were holding taught people to ignore amber.) A temperature or humidity in band but within 15 % of the band's width of an edge is amber only when the machine that should act is not acting, or when the reading has stayed near that edge for 15 min (its trace tells); otherwise it shows the calm "In band". The machine that should act: humidity low, the humidifier; humidity high, a fitted dehumidifier (or the humidifier, which should have stopped); temperature high, the aircon cooling; temperature low, the aircon not cooling. (2026-10-29) A machine that has not reached its own switch point is acting as told: humidity near low counts as not acting only at or under the humidifier's on-point with the humidifier off, humidity near high only at the band's top (the dehumidifier's on-point) with the dehumidifier off, or at or over the humidifier's off-point with the humidifier still on. A machine the room does not have (or not known) never counts as not acting, so such a reading turns amber only after 15 min there. The words fit one line: "Near low", "Near high", with "· falling" or "· rising" when the trend runs toward that edge (web/band-math.js `nearChip`, the same on the Overview and the room page). Out of band is amber, a fault red. (2026-10-29, owner: "OK" beside an amber "Near high" read as a contradiction.) On the Overview a room with no alarm, nothing out of band and in Auto but with an amber near-edge reading takes an amber "Watch" pill, not "OK"; it does not count as needing attention, and the status line names it ("3 rooms OK · Room 1 humidity near high") or counts several ("2 rooms to watch") (web/overview-math.js `nearEdges`). (2026-10-29, owner: the Overview flapped and reordered as the machines cycled.) The room cards keep one order, by name, whatever their state. The pill and the status line say "Out of band" only once a reading has been out as long as its alarm waits (5 min; humidity over the band 15 min; CO₂ at the safety level 1 min) and "Watch" once it has been near an edge for 2 min; until then, and for 2 min after it is back, the room stays as it was. The reading's own words show at once, without the amber until then (`settleRooms`). On opening the page a reading out of band counts as held only when its last 30 min trace bucket was out of band too (an air exchange wets a room for a few minutes). The status line's polite live region speaks only when its words change.

rules.name: The Exchange Words Rule
rules.body: CO₂ has no band to stay in: its two numbers are where the air exchange starts and stops, so its status says what the exchange is doing (web/band-math.js `co2Status`, the same on the Overview, the reading card and the drawing). Below the stop point and "Exchange off" are green; "Exchange running" is neutral (`ink-2`), never amber; "Over the start point" with the exchange not running is amber; within 15 % of the gap from the start point to the safety level "Near the safety level" is amber; at the safety level red. On the Overview "Exchange off" carries its start point ("Exchange off · starts at 1,400 ppm"): a high reading with the exchange off is then not read as a contradiction.

rules.name: The Units Rule
rules.body: Every number on screen carries its unit, the controller's reasons included ("CO₂ 744 ppm between 700 and 800 ppm"), and the reasons compare in words, never in maths signs ("RH 87.9 %, at or under its on-point 88 %", "CO₂ 1,450 ppm, at or over 1,400 ppm"); thousands are grouped (1,000 ppm); a range of dates takes an en dash. A number never parts from its unit at a wrap and a '·' keeps to the words before it, so a wrap leaves it at a line's end and no line starts with '·' (a no-break space before it, a normal one after: web/text-math.js `keepLines`, `DOT`; 2026-10-29c, a line began "· fresh air every 12 min."). An aircon is entered and shown in kW; its BTU/h class (the size shops sell) is a picker and a note in brackets, never the input's unit.

rules.name: The By-Hand Rule
rules.body: A value a person set that differs from the program (a band changed on Setup) is shown in the accent text colour with the program's own value under it ("stage: 900 ppm") and a way back ("Back to stage values"): a choice, not a warning. Three places say it: the Setup inputs, the Crop tab's current stage and, in a line under the Now tab's Control head, "Bands changed by hand on Setup" with its own Back to stage values (2026-10-29c) (web/crop-math.js `byHandValues`, `stageBody`); while they agree nothing shows.

rules.name: The Navigation Rule
rules.body: The top bar holds the farm's name, Live, the theme, Today (with its count), Calendar, Harvest, Overview and Settings, and a red alarm button only while there are alarms; on a phone the links are their icons and, with too little room for it (about 400 px wide since Calendar, 2026-11-03), the farm's name shows as its mark alone. (2026-11-04, Harvest: under 400 px the top links and the theme button are 40 px wide and 44 px tall, so six icons fit at 360 px with the mark; under 380 px, while the alarm button shows, the farm's mark is hidden, as there is no room for it.) (2026-11-05, the task grid audit: from 601 to 899 px the five worded links left the mark 22 px under "Live" and the page scrolling sideways at 700 px, so up to 899 px the links are their icons, 44 px wide, the Today count kept, as on a phone; from 900 px they carry their words. With the alarm button showing, 900 to about 1000 px keeps the 28 px mark without the farm's name.) The Overview holds every room (the Rooms list is folded into it) and Add room; a room is reached from its card or the room switch on its page.

rules.name: The One Format Rule
rules.body: A quantity has one formatter and every tab uses it: humidity and filter pressure to one decimal (91.2 % RH, 40.2 Pa), metric units with a space before them, ranges with an en dash (19–21 °C). If two tabs could disagree about a number, they share the formatter.

rules.name: The 44 px Rule
rules.body: On a phone every control is at least 44 px tall (and an icon button 44 px wide, 40 px under 400 px): buttons, fields, selects, link chips, tabs, a fold's summary, a link that is a row's only way in, a checkbox's words. A desk keeps the compact heights (36 px buttons, 40 px fields, 32 px compact buttons). Where a target cannot grow without moving the layout, its padding grows and a negative margin of the same size keeps the spacing.

rules.name: The Readings First Rule
rules.body: On a phone the order is readings, alarms, control, machines, the drawing, then the crop: the question "is the room OK" is answered before any scroll.

rules.name: The One Card Level Rule
rules.body: There is never a card inside a card. Parts that would nest become cards themselves (each Crop stage, the Stages list and the program row are sibling cards) or hairline-separated sections inside one card (the Control groups, the Machines rows, the Setup status footer as a 1 px top rule, not a box).

rules.name: The Picture Rule
rules.body: A picture says what a thing is, never how it is: no green, amber, red or accent blue in it, nothing in it changes with a reading or a machine's state (the pills and words keep the state), and it always sits beside words that say the same, so it is `aria-hidden`. A closed task's or an unfitted machine's picture fades with its words. A test checks that every crop, rule, machine and sensor has one and that no picture holds a fixed colour or a state token.

dos: Do spend colour on state only: `accent` for selection, primary action and running; green in band; amber warning; red fault.
Do keep temperature, humidity and CO₂ in their series hues (`--s-t`, `--s-rh`, `--s-co2`) on every trace and chart of that quantity, on both the Now and History tabs.
Do keep one filled button per view or panel; show On as a tint.
Do make every part that would nest either a sibling card or a hairline-separated section.
Do set every number in tabular figures, with one formatter per quantity (humidity and filter pressure to one decimal) and metric units.
Do add every new colour to both theme blocks under one name.
Do write labels and states in plain English sentence case: name the machine, the number and the unit.

Do build a new page from the parts above (card, card head, rows, tiles, the data table, the segmented control, chips, folds, messages, empty states) before writing a new one; a module's CSS uses the tokens and these parts' classes and adds only what is its own.
Do set every size from the `--fs-*` steps and every corner from the six radius steps; every control 44 px on a phone.
donts: Don't put a card inside a card.
Don't colour icons, headings or target labels to decorate; the Crop tab's target icons stay `muted`.
Don't use a series hue for state, a button or body text.
Don't fill an On switch with solid accent beside a Send or Save.
Don't add shadows to dark-theme cards or depth effects beyond the vocabulary above.
Don't add gradients, shadows or hatching to the room drawing, or change what it represents.
Don't colour a picture by state, or let a picture say something its words do not.
Don't show a quantity in two formats on two tabs, or any US unit.
Don't make a second version of a part that exists (another chip, another segmented control, another table style, another chevron); change the one part, for every page.
Don't set a size in `rem`, under 12 px, or a weight other than 400, 500, 600 and 700.
Don't title a section card at the Name size; Name is for a thing's own card.
